scope: feature branch 004-stripe-app vs origin/main (correctness+spec, security, documentation lenses)

findings.claim: No test would fail if the row lock in Customer.sync() were removed, so the concurrency guarantee the plan requires (ARCH-004) is unverified.
findings.evidence: tests/test_stripe/test_models.py:404-414 asserts only that the first non-SAVEPOINT query is a SELECT on mvp_payments_stripe_customer. SQLite never emits FOR UPDATE, and no other test mentions select_for_update (grep of tests/ finds none). mvp_payments/stripe/models.py:147 carries the lock.
findings.reproduction: Change `Customer.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=self.pk)` to `Customer.objects.get(pk=self.pk)` at models.py:147 and run `uv run pytest tests/test_stripe`. The suite stays green (373 passed on the unmutated branch; the SELECT-first test passes either way).
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the lock itself. Patch or spy `QuerySet.select_for_update` in the existing test, or check `queries` for `FOR UPDATE` when `connection.features.has_select_for_update` is true. The repaired test must fail under the mutation of dropping select_for_update().

findings.claim: sync() reads only the first item of each subscription, and fails with IndexError on one with no items. Neither is documented.
findings.evidence: mvp_payments/stripe/models.py:170 and :175 use `subscription["items"]["data"][0]`. A subscription with two items records the first item's price, amount and period and ignores the rest. A subscription with an empty items list raises IndexError, which the webhook does not catch (views.py:53 catches only stripe.StripeError). The webhook answers 500 and Stripe retries the event indefinitely.
findings.reproduction: Respond to GET /v1/subscriptions with a subscription whose items.data is [] and deliver customer.subscription.updated: the view returns a 500 and the whole sync for that customer fails, including its other subscriptions.
findings.suggested_fix: State in docs/reference/stripe-app.md (Records > Subscription) that only a subscription's first item is recorded. Skip a subscription with no items rather than failing the whole customer. Stripe's pricing table creates single-item subscriptions, so this is not reachable today.

findings.claim: Customer.signature() is a public static method with no docstring, against the code-documentation standard.
findings.evidence: mvp_payments/stripe/models.py:79-81. It is not a framework-hook override, so it needs Args:/Returns:. client_reference() and from_checkout() depend on it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a docstring with Args (pk) and Returns (the hex HMAC), or make it private (`_signature`) if it is not meant as a public interface.

findings.claim: Customer.sync() holds the customer row lock across every Stripe round trip (customer, subscription list, one call per distinct product), and the webhook wraps that in a further transaction.
findings.evidence: mvp_payments/stripe/models.py:145-200 and views.py:49-52. On PostgreSQL, a slow or hung Stripe call keeps the customer row locked for the SDK timeout, and a concurrent event for the same customer blocks behind it. Correct behaviour, but it widens the lock window.
findings.suggested_fix: None required. Optionally fetch from Stripe first and take the lock only for the writes, but that reopens the older-state-overwrites-newer window the lock closes, so leave it unless contention is seen. Worth a sentence in the reference's `Customer.sync()` section.

notes: Searched names: Customer.sync (4 references: views, command, from_checkout path, tests, all consistent), Customer.client_reference/from_checkout (3 non-test references, only docs and views call them; no page passes the reference yet, which the spec defers), SubscriptionQuerySet.for_user/subscribed (2 non-test references, docs only), API_VERSION (client.py only), mvp_payments.urls change (1 reference, namespace 'payments' matches APP_NAMESPACE and docs), removed `mypy_path` and removed `stripe<8` pin (no other references; mypy and ruff pass), demo/urls.py no longer mounts drf_stripe.urls (grep shows no remaining reverse of its URL names). Not searched: templates outside mvp_payments/ and demo/ for use of the removed drf_stripe API routes.

Tests swept for cannot-fail shapes: about 190 new or changed tests across tests/test_stripe/*, test_app.py, test_demo.py and test_factories.py. One finding (REV-001). The signature, hostile-reference, secret-leak and 400/500 tests assert specific statuses and records and read as sound. Full suite: 373 passed. Stripe app coverage 99-100% (models.py line 155 uncovered: the `raise` for a non-resource_missing error, patch coverage well above 85%). ruff and mypy clean.

Security lens: signature verified before any read (views.py:41, header=None/''/garbage all raise SignatureVerificationError, probed against stripe 16). An empty secret answers 500 and never verifies. No secret in logs, admin, templates, checks or command output (error types only). Hostile client_reference_id is rejected by constant_time_compare before pk reaches the ORM: no underscore, empty parts, non-numeric or huge pk, mismatched or foreign signature all return None. The reference is HMAC-SHA256 under SECRET_KEY with an app-specific salt, so a signature for another purpose cannot pass. Admin: add/change refused for all, delete refused on the app's own pages (url_name prefix 'mvp_payments_stripe_'), cascade from the user admin still allowed; a staff user with delete rights on users but not on Stripe models is blocked from deleting users who have a customer, which is the cost the docs state. A concurrent duplicate checkout event can raise IntegrityError on Customer creation, giving 500 and a Stripe retry, which converges.

Documentation lens: opened all five new pages, the README section and the ADR, and checked examples against the code. Imports, URL name payments:stripe-webhook, event list, status codes, field list, JPY and USD formatting, command options and error behaviour all match. The reference and docstring say the reference holds only letters, digits and underscores, while ADR 0011 says the pricing table also accepts dashes. The code produces only digits, underscores and hex, so both are true of the output.

Postgres sorts NULLs first under `-current_period_end`, so `.first()` could return a row with a NULL period before a dated one. Stripe always sends a period for the statuses that count, so it is not reachable today.

demo/apps.py imports stripe and sets the module-level stripe.api_version for drf-stripe-subscription. This is demo code outside mvp_payments/, so FR-001 and SC-005 (which scan the package) hold, and the comment says why.
Spec fidelity: FR-001 to FR-021 and SC-001 to SC-008 each map to a passing test or a documented page. FR-013 (current subscription) is met by `.subscribed().first()` and documented.
